sector: Industrials — Aerospace & Defense — eVTOL / Advanced Air Mobility
research_status_text: Post-earnings update (Q2 and Q3 2026; Boeing Wisk/Insitu/SkyGrid deal pending close)
stance_text: Watch — unchanged; value lowered because cash use runs about 30% above the July base and the Boeing deal adds about 155 million shares
lens_text: End-2029 enterprise value of the combined company plus cash less debt, on shares after the Boeing deal, vendor and award shares, and the equity raises needed to end 2029 with a year of cash at each scenario's spending rate; three-year value, undiscounted

bear.basis: Type certification slips past 2029; cash use cut to $750M a year; $1.86B raised at $2.00; end-2029 EV $600M (Insitu about 1.6x its roughly $240M of revenue, plus about $200M of IP; total revenue about $260M) + $750M cash - $93M debt = $1,257M on 2,065M shares

base.basis: Midnight certified 2028-29 and flying in a few cities, Thunder in early defense orders, 2029 revenue about $450M; cash use $1.0B a year (standalone about $860M plus Wisk net of Insitu profit); $2.86B raised at $5.00; end-2029 EV $9.0B (about 20x revenue, about 40x ex-Insitu) + $1,000M cash - $93M debt on 1,658M shares

bull.basis: Certification 2028, LA28 service, Thunder program of record, 2029 revenue $900M; cash use $800M a year net of defense revenue; $1.86B raised at $10.00 plus $200M from both Boeing warrants; end-2029 EV $25B (about 28x revenue) + $800M cash - $93M debt on 1,236M shares

horizon_text: End-2029 value, undiscounted; dilution from raises, vendor shares and awards counted in the share count
thesis: Archer is moving forward operationally (final FAA type-certification phase, a Market Survey certificate for Los Angeles operations, Anduril engine deliveries, a Boeing deal that brings Insitu's $200M-plus of profitable revenue), but operating cash use, capital spending and vendor shares come to about $0.93 billion a year, so $1.35 billion lasts six to seven quarters rather than the 3.6 years the July call assumed. Every path needs about $2-3 billion of new equity before 2030 on top of about 155 million deal shares. If Midnight is certified in 2028-29 and the combined company is worth $9 billion at the end of 2029, the stock is worth about $6.
consensus_view: No Street snapshot was captured. The stock rose to $6.97 after the Boeing deal was announced and has given all of that back, closing at $4.71; at that price the post-deal company is valued at about $3.15 billion of enterprise value, of which Insitu is about $0.4 billion at 2x revenue. Management frames the deal as the start of a diversified aerospace and defense platform with Insitu revenue offsetting Midnight spending.
variant_view: The July call measured runway on operating cash flow alone; counting capital spending and vendor share issuances, the burn is about $0.93 billion a year before Wisk, and the next raise comes in 2027-28, not 2029-30. We expect year-end 2026 liquidity near $1.14 billion and an equity raise of at least $500 million announced in 2027, priced below the $6.29-$6.97 closes seen after the deal announcement. The more important disagreement is calibration: the July call put a quarter of the probability on a bull that needs 98th-percentile growth.

low_score_reasons: valuation: the base raises $2.86B, 53% of the pre-raise market cap, at $5.00, above today's $4.71; the bull assumes less cash use ($800M) than the base while certifying and running LA28 service; the base's $9.0B is about 40x 2029 non-Insitu revenue; Own starts at about a 19% bull weight.

variant_view: the disagreement the call says matters most ('calibration') is with its own July backfill, not the market; the testable claims (year-end liquidity, a $500M-plus 2027 raise) are close to what holders already expect.

risk: after base cash use rose to $1.0B, the kill criterion, pre-mortem signal and change-my-mind trigger equal the base assumption, and the base's implied gross Wisk spending sits at or above the $150M catalyst line.

calibration: base rates are applied to the bull only; the 86th-percentile base keeps 50%; the '$10 raise' is part of the bull, not a separate hurdle; the reference class is five-year CAGRs of companies with revenue, applied to a three-year pro forma path.
review.counter_case: Apply the call's own calibration argument consistently and the stance is Avoid, not Watch. A base case at the 86th percentile of its size bucket should not carry 50%. A $2.86B raise worth 53% of the market cap is more likely priced below today's $4.71 than at $5.00. Pricing it at $4.00 cuts the base to $5.50, and at 50/40/10 the fair value is $4.59, a -0.9% annual return. Base cash use of $1.0B a year already sits on the call's own kill line, so any Wisk overrun pushes the next raise toward the bear's $2.00, where 928M new shares nearly double the post-deal count.
review.response: Accepted the corrections: the burn is $0.93B a year on the true nine-month figures; the $126.8M is labeled as the roll-forward's stock-based compensation line; the Action says $2-3 billion of new equity; the kill criterion, pre-mortem signal and change-my-mind trigger move to $1.15B ($290M a quarter), above the $1.0B base; the Wisk catalyst moves to $250M against about $160M gross in the base. The note now shows a $4.00 base raise: base $5.50, fair value $6.08, 8.9% a year, still Watch. On the counter-case: the base is the path where certification arrives as management describes it, so its growth is mostly Insitu plus the first eVTOL and defense revenue rather than organic growth at a mature firm, and the reference class overstates how rare it is; we keep it at 50%. Moving to 50/40/10 with a $4.00 raise would need the bear to be as likely as the base, which no event since July supports: the program reached the final certification phase and gained Boeing as its largest holder. We record the Avoid case here and in the sensitivities; a raise below $3.00 or a missed piloted transition by March 2027 would move us there.
